title: P99 stitching and ghost-stage investigation
content:
Summary:
This is a working investigation into a recurring class of high-p99 end-to-end responses we observed in the last two weeks for REST/chat endpoints. Symptoms are long tails (p99 >> p95) where standard stage-level telemetry shows no single dominant stage — instead there is an extra ~200–800ms unaccounted-for component that appears intermittently. We label this phenomenon 'ghost-stage' and hypothesize it is caused by cross-stage handoffs + trace stitching gaps (async batch handoffs, rpc timeouts, or scheduling stalls on host VMs).

Scope and cohorts:
- Time window: 2025-10-30 -> 2025-11-06 (synthetic spike + steady production).
- Routes examined: /v1/chat/stream (mostly tokenized prompt workloads), /v1/complete (short prompts).
- Cohorts:
  - cohort-A (short-seq): seq_len<=128, ~60% of traffic
  - cohort-B (med-seq): 129<=seq_len<=512, ~30%
  - cohort-C (long-seq): seq_len>512, ~10% (disproportionate p99 contribution)

Sampling methodology:
- Stochastic trace sampler targeting responses >= 99th percentile by route (trace sampling rate varied: 1% baseline, 100% when p99 alarm fires).
- Stitch traces across services using trace_id + event correlation; we added sticky tagging for async-batch boundaries to help identify incomplete spans.
- For this doc we used aggregated telemetry from: local dev replay, prod-sampled traces, and a replay job (tools/trace-replay --group ghost-detect --window 7d).

Observed metrics (aggregated):
- cohort-A: p50=48ms, p95=132ms, p99=273ms
- cohort-B: p50=92ms, p95=248ms, p99=512ms
- cohort-C: p50=210ms, p95=640ms, p99=1.18s
- Note: p99 weight heavily skewed to cohort-C (70% of p99 events) even though it is only 10% of requests.

Representative trace (example id: trace-20251104-8237):
- total wall: 0.374s (374ms)
- tokenization: 4ms
- request-parse: 6ms
- precompile/model-setup: 12ms
- kv-cache lookup (hit): 18ms
- batch-wait (async evict batcher): 82ms
- GPU-inference (kernel+streams): 205ms
- emit-serialize: 16ms
- egress/response-send: 9ms
- observation: the 'batch-wait' span here is fully instrumented. Ghost-stage in this sample is not visible.

Ghost-stage example (trace id: trace-20251103-1992):
- total wall: 1.02s (1020ms)
- tokenization: 5ms
- model-setup: 11ms
- kv-cache lookup (miss): 42ms
- GPU-inference: 212ms
- emit-serialize: 18ms
- egress: 7ms
- reported stage sum: 295ms
- unaccounted / ghost delta: ~725ms (this is the anomaly)
- additional note: there are two short rpc spans to the async-batcher service but their recorded durations are ~4–8ms each — they do not sum to the delta.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Trace stitching gaps across process boundaries (lost/wrongly-timestamped spans) cause missing latency attribution.
2) Hidden queueing in the host VM (scheduler preemption, GC, CPU steal) that isn't captured by application spans.
3) Network egress stalls / NAT gateway retries outside our tracing window.
4) Batcher backpressure that manifests as external scheduling (batcher worker being descheduled) — spans present but not reflecting wait due to instrumentation boundaries.
5) Model runtime transient JIT/compilation path (rare) that adds hundreds of ms in cold pockets.

What we tested and results:
- Trace-stitching accuracy test: replayed a set of 5k p99 traces through trace-replayer with full tracing enabled. Outcome: ~12% of traces showed missing parent events attributable to a race where the span parentId got overwritten for async handoffs. Patch PR #4213 adds deterministic parent inheritance for queued messages.
- Host-level observability: correlated p99 events with host metrics (CPU steal, I/O wait). Outcome: ~18% of ghost events had spikes in cpu_steal or high iowait on the host (particularly on Shared-GPU VMs).
- Network egress probes: ran synthetic egress probes during a 24h window. Outcome: <1% probes show transient 200–300ms outbound delays; not sufficient to explain majority of events.
- Batcher worker scheduling stress test (killing one worker at a time): reproduced multi-hundred-ms gaps when worker was paused for >200ms. This reproduces the ghost delta in the lab.
- JIT/compilation traces: rare cold-compile recorded; accounted for <3% of p99 events.

Takeaways so far:
- The ghost-stage is multi-causal. Primary contributors: (a) trace-stitching race that makes some handoff waits invisible, (b) host scheduling preemption on some instance types, and (c) rare batcher-worker stalls.
- Fixing instrumentation alone reduces 'unaccounted' mass by ~45% in replayed traces. Combining with instance-type hardening reduces p99 by another ~25%.

Immediate action items (owner in parens):
- Merge PR #4213 (deterministic parent inheritance) into canary branch and run replay validation (Liam).
- Run a 72h canary with instance-type pinned to 'dedicated-gpu-v5' for high-p99 routes (Marta).
- Add host scheduler metrics to trace payload (docker: /proc/schedstat snapshot) and correlate in trace aggregator (Noah).
- Create a lightweight agent check for batcher-worker thrashing and alert if worker loop latency > 150ms for >1 minute (eng-infra).

Repro commands and artifacts:
- Replay job: ./tools/trace-replay --cohort ghost-detect --from 2025-10-30 --to 2025-11-06 --full-trace --out replay-results/nov-ghost
- Profiling harness for worker stalls: ./bench/batcher-stress --workers 32 --pause-ms 250 --measure stall-avg --out /tmp/stall-samples
- Quick grep for ghost traces: jq -r '.traces[] | select(.total - (.stages | add) > 0.2) | .id' traces-2025-11-*.ndjson

Open questions:
- What fraction of ghost events map to customers on Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private? Early signal: Hosted (shared) instances show higher incidence. Need RBAC/tenant mapping (security check required).
- Could garbage collection in language runtimes used by batcher be contributing? We only have coarse metrics today.
- Are specific model sizes more prone due to different batcher code paths?

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- 11/04: found first reproducible ghost in lab via worker pause test.
- 11/09: trace-replay shows 12% missing parents; patch authored.
- 11/14: canary started for deterministic parent inheritance; need replay validation.

Appendix: short checklist for reviewers:
- Verify PR #4213 unit tests + added e2e trace test.
- Confirm replay job config used same sampling seed as prod-sample.
- Validate host metric collection additions do not add >1% overhead to trace payload.

TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] deploy stitched tracing patch to canary -> verify ghost delta reduction via replay
- [ ] pin canary subset of traffic to dedicated instances and compare incidence
- [ ] add batcher-worker thrash alert and run for 48h
- [ ] update runbook with 'ghost-stage' detection heuristics and example traces

If you take anything from this doc: focus on trace-parent correctness + host scheduler signals. Both together give the best leverage to eliminate the unaccounted mass in p99 events.
